What Should You Know About Buffalo County And This Guide

Buffalo County sits in central Nebraska with Kearney as the county seat. It blends a college town feel, farm ground, and steady housing demand. This guide walks you through how tax sales work in Buffalo County, Nebraska. You will learn when the sale happens, how the auction runs, what returns to expect, and where to find official links.

What Is Buffalo County, Nebraska Tax Lien Investing

Nebraska uses tax lien certificates rather than tax deed sales. When owners fall behind on property taxes, the county treasurer sells tax lien certificates at a public sale. Investors pay the delinquent taxes and receive a certificate that earns interest until the owner redeems. If the owner does not redeem within the three-year redemption period, the investor can start a treasurer’s deed or court foreclosure process under Nebraska law. 

What Are The Important Tax Sale Details

Key Buffalo County Tax Sale Facts

Key Takeaways

  • Buffalo County, Nebraska, utilizes tax lien certificates for properties with delinquent taxes, offering a structured investment opportunity.
  • Tax sales occur annually on the first Monday in March, with a three-year redemption period and a fourteen percent interest rate on unpaid taxes.
  • Investors must conduct thorough research and due diligence before bidding to avoid costly mistakes and ensure profitable returns.
  • Buffalo County is open to both local and foreign investors, provided they meet registration requirements and understand local laws.
  • The county’s strong economy, housing demand, and educational institutions support a viable environment for tax lien investing.

What Fun Facts Help You Understand Buffalo County

  • Buffalo County was created in the eighteen fifties and organized in eighteen seventy.
  • The county is named for the American bison that once roamed the Great Plains.
  • Kearney is the county seat and one of the larger cities in Nebraska.
  • The county covers about nine hundred sixty-eight square miles with several small towns.

These points matter because they show long-term settlement and steady growth, which can support real estate demand and tax lien opportunities.

What Are The Main Attractions And Economic Highlights

  • Attractions include the Great Platte River Road Archway, local museums, and Platte River recreation areas near Kearney.
  • Transport access comes from Interstate eighty, US highways, and nearby regional air service in Kearney.
  • Key industries include health care, retail trade, manufacturing, and higher education through the University of Nebraska at Kearney.
  • Community life includes college events, farm-related business, and outdoor activities along the Platte River.

Why Is Buffalo County A Good Place For Tax Lien Investors

  • The county population is large enough to support an active tax base and regular sales.
  • Fourteen percent legal interest on tax lien redemptions offers high returns compared to many savings products.
  • Three-year redemption gives owners time to pay while giving investors a clear time frame.
  • Properties back the liens, so investors hold a claim that is ahead of many other debts under Nebraska law.

How Does The Buffalo County Tax Lien Auction Work

Buffalo County holds its public tax sale at the courthouse on the first Monday in March at nine in the morning Central Time. Check-in runs from eight to eight forty-five at the treasurer’s office. 

Registration begins the Monday before the sale. Investors must submit a completed Buffalo County tax sale registration form, a W-9, a twenty-five-dollar nonrefundable registration fee per bidder, and a blank check for certificate purchases. Nebraska statute requires this registration fee for each bidder. 

The sale uses a round robin format. The county draws random bidder numbers on Thursday morning before the sale for all registered bidders. There is a limit of twenty-five bid numbers per company or individual. On the Wednesday before the sale, the county posts an updated list of parcels on the Buffalo County website in dollar descending order. Everyone must use this updated list during the sale. 

During the auction, the treasurer calls parcels in the order of the county list. Each bidder number gets a turn in sequence. When it is your turn, you may claim one or more parcels by paying the full advertised delinquent taxes and related charges. If you pass, the next bidder number in the round robin gets a chance. There are no refunds after the sale, so knowing the property before you bid is very important. 

How Does The Auction Work Step By Step

Here is a simple step-by-step look at how the Buffalo County tax lien auction works.

  1. Review the Delinquent Tax List

    Review the delinquent tax list for Buffalo County on Nebraska Taxes Online and the county website.

  2. Complete the Registration Process

    Complete the Buffalo County registration form and W-9, then pay the twenty-five-dollar fee

  3. Check In and Bring a Blank Check

    Bring a blank check for certificate purchases and check in at the treasurer’s office before the sale.

  4. Receive Your Bidder Number

    Receive your bidder number after the Thursday random draw or at check-in if allowed that year.

  5. Claim Parcels During the Round Robin

    During the round robin, claim parcels when your number is called by agreeing to pay the full delinquent amount

  6. Wait for Certificates and Receipts

    After the sale, the treasurer’s office processes tax sale certificates and mails copies and receipts, while holding the originals


What Returns Can You Expect From Buffalo County Tax Lien Certificates

Buffalo County tax lien certificates pay fourteen percent interest per year on the tax amount and subsequent taxes you pay, from the date the certificate is processed until the date of redemption. Interest stops on the redemption date. Registration fees and certificate fees are not refunded. 

Real returns depend on how long the owner takes to redeem. Many redemptions occur within the first one to two years, which can still give an attractive yield on a cash investment. If the owner never redeems within the three-year redemption period, you can seek a treasurer’s deed or start a foreclosure case with help from a local attorney. 

Are Buffalo County Tax Sales Open To Foreign Investors

Nebraska law does not limit participation to county residents. Many counties, including Buffalo, allow any legally formed person or business to register as long as they submit the required forms and registration fee. That makes Buffalo County open to investors from other states and from outside the United States, provided they can supply a valid tax form and follow United States reporting rules. 

Foreign investors should work through a tax advisor on currency, tax treaty, and filing questions. You will need a United States tax identification number to complete the W nine and receive interest payments correctly.

Why Is Due Diligence So Important In Buffalo County Tax Lien Investing

Buffalo County tax sale buyers must research each parcel before bidding. The county clearly states that it is the buyer’s responsibility to know what they are buying and that there are no refunds. Certificates are sold under Nebraska law, and mistakes can be costly. 

What Does Good Due Diligence Include

  • Pull the parcel on Nebraska Taxes Online and confirm the correct property and tax years.
  • Use the county assessor’s parcel map to check location, land use, and basic property data.
  • Check aerial maps and street views where available to see access, nearby uses, and condition.
  • Search court and register of deeds records for mortgages, liens, and other legal claims that may survive a tax sale.
  • Estimate repair costs and end value if you might later foreclose and own the property.

What Are The Risks If You Skip Due Diligence

  • You might buy a parcel with no legal access, flood issues, or unusable land.
  • Senior liens, special assessments, or federal liens can survive and cut into your profit.
  • Improvements might be gone, leaving only land value under your tax lien.
  • Foreclosure or treasurer’s deed costs can be high and may not match the property value.
  • You can lose time and money if a title problem blocks resale or refinance.

Can You Buy Over-The-Counter Liens In Buffalo County

Nebraska law allows county treasurers to sell remaining tax lien certificates at private sale after the public auction, once the treasurer has filed the public sale return. Many Nebraska counties treat this as a year-round private sale list.

In practice, Buffalo County may have unsold taxes that can be purchased later in person through the treasurer’s office. Selection changes during the year. Always confirm current rules with the treasurer staff and ask whether they keep a private sale list for investors. 

How Do You Purchase Over-the-Counter Liens Or Deeds

Call or email the Buffalo County treasurer’s office and ask if a private tax sale list is available. If they offer one, review the parcels and follow the same research steps you would use for the public sale. Once you choose parcels, the treasurer will quote amounts due. You then pay the delinquent taxes, certificate fee, and any required charges so the office can issue a tax sale certificate in your name. 

What Are The Benefits of Over-the-Counter Purchases

Over-the-counter liens give you more time to research each parcel. You avoid the pressure of an auction room and round robin bidding. You can also pick smaller liens or special cases that other bidders skipped. That approach can work well if you prefer careful study and a slower pace. 

Why Is Buffalo County A Strong Choice For Tax Lien Investors

What Economic And Tax Advantages Stand Out

  • Buffalo County has one of the largest county populations in Nebraska, which supports regular property turnover and tax collections.
  • The University of Nebraska at Kearney and local health care centers help keep jobs and housing demand steady.
  • Nebraska offers a clear three-year redemption period and a statewide fourteen percent interest rate on real property tax liens.

What Should You Know About The Real Estate Market

  • Kearney supports single-family homes, student rentals, and small multifamily units, which creates a mix of tax lien sizes.
  • Rural parts of Buffalo County include farm ground and small towns, where liens may be lower in face value but still carry the same interest rate.
  • Investors who track both the city parcels and the rural parcels can find a range of risk and return profiles inside one county.

What Is The Bottom Line For Buffalo County Tax Lien Investing

Buffalo County, Nebraska, offers a clear tax lien system, set by state law and detailed local rules. The annual public tax sale on the first Monday in March, the three-year redemption period, and the fourteen percent interest rate create strong investment potential for patient buyers. 

Success still depends on research and planning. You need to study parcels, understand local property values, and have a plan for each certificate if it does not redeem. When you follow the county rules and add solid due diligence, Buffalo County tax liens can be a solid part of a larger real estate investment plan.

What Pro Tips Help You Succeed In Buffalo County

  • Treat the updated Wednesday parcel list as your main working list and mark it with notes on value, access, and use.
  • Sort the list by neighborhood or town rather than by dollar amount so you can build simple farm, town, and city strategies.
  • Track repeat delinquent owners over several years, since frequent delinquency can point to longer redemptions or future foreclosure chances.
  • Start with a small set of parcels near Kearney where you can easily gather sales data, then move into rural parcels once you gain experience.
  • Build a local team that includes a Buffalo County real estate agent, closing company, and attorney so you can move quickly when a lien is ready for foreclosure or deed.

What Questions Do Investors Often Ask About Buffalo County Tax Liens

What happens if the owner does not redeem the tax lien?

After three years, you can start the legal steps to get a treasurer’s deed or foreclose.

Do I own the property after three years?

No. You must complete the legal process before ownership transfers.

Can other liens survive the tax lien sale?

Yes. Federal liens and some local charges may remain.

Can I access the property during redemption?

No. The owner keeps possession until you legally receive a deed.

Can I sell my tax lien certificate?

Yes. Nebraska allows lien transfers through the county treasurer.
